items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s how we continued as Lambert, Hendricks, and Bavan for two years.

ctx.x: 1,000 people could come to America from Ireland alone, but only 100 could come from all Asia and Africa. That was the McCaren-Walter Immigration Act. That way they packed the country with Irish people who were Catholic, so you were going to have a right-wing constituency there, which is why we’re in the political shape that we’re in now. You got these moral midgets like Newt Gingrich cropping up in Pennsylvania and going to Georgia, where they’re stupid enough to vote for him and have him talk

about the morality of the country while he serves his wife with divorce papers after her mastectomy. These people are impossible. But that’s how they got constituency into the country, that act. Because Yolande had been trying for four years. So we went to the State Department and certified that we had gainful employment for her, and she got in. That’s how that started. That’s how we continued as Lambert, Hendricks, and Bavan for two years. Then I left.
